The direction bug below does not happen to create a cycle in this small graph, which is exactly why it is dangerous: it passes both schema validation and cycle_check while still being semantically wrong.

findings.gate: Edge direction — depends-on must be prerequisite -> dependent
findings.detail: The edge {from: approver-dashboard-service, to: claim-submission-service, type: depends-on} is REVERSED. impact-assessment.md's own Components Identified rationale for approver-dashboard-service states explicitly: 'needs submitted claims to exist before it has anything to display — claim-submission-service is a hard prerequisite for approver-dashboard-service, not the other way round.' The edge must read {from: claim-submission-service, to: approver-dashboard-service, type: depends-on}. This is the same class of bug phase-1/README.md documents an earlier worked-example revision shipping with: blocks edges ran the correct blocker->blocked direction while the depends-on edge ran dependent->prerequisite — schema-valid, semantically wrong.

Because the direction bug in FND-02 makes claim-submission-service falsely appear to be gated by approver-dashboard-service, the generator's declared critical_path (corporate-sso-provider -> approver-dashboard-service -> claim-submission-service) is a real but WRONG 2-edge path built on the reversed edge. After correcting the edge direction, the independently re-derived longest blocking chain is corporate-sso-provider -> claim-submission-service -> approver-dashboard-service — still 2 edges, but the node order (and the real-world build sequence it implies) is reversed from what the generator declared.

fixes_applied.description: Corrected the reversed depends-on edge's from/to to match impact-assessment.md's own stated prerequisite rationale, then re-ran the longest-path computation over the corrected edge set. Re-saved dependency-graph.json at the SAME s3 location (artifact-c3d4e5f6, s3://adlc-artifacts/exec-c3d4e5f6/dependency-graph.json) with both the corrected edge and the corrected critical_path — items and the saved file were updated together, per this agent's own retrieve-fix-resave discipline.
fixes_applied.after: edges: [..., {"from": "claim-submission-service", "to": "approver-dashboard-service", "type": "depends-on"}, ...]; critical_path.nodes: ["corporate-sso-provider", "claim-submission-service", "approver-dashboard-service"]; critical_path.rationale: "Longest blocking chain is 2 edges: corporate-sso-provider -> claim-submission-service -> approver-dashboard-service, corrected from a reversed depends-on edge that had inverted the real build order."
